policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Ketiv וידעו and qere וְיֹדְעָיו differ only in the orthography of the 3ms suffix on the plural participle (defective ו- vs. plene יו-); both read 'those who know him'. ASV 'they that know him' renders that sense with no italicized supply and cannot separate the spellings. The only note is alternative_rendering (a different construal of the whole verse) and does not decide a reading. Base qere fallback retained.

Ketiv יקצירו (hiphil) and qere יִקְצוֹרוּ (qal) of קצר both yield 'they reap/cut'; ASV 'They cut their provender in the field' has no wording or italics that requires one stem over the other. The note 'Or, his' is alternative_rendering on the possessive of 'provender' and does not bear on this unit. Base qere fallback retained.
